question: Supplier S-104 will miss its next ship date. Handle it.
answer:
S-104's late shipment hits Lacrivia hardest at the East distribution centre (DC-EAST), which has only 1–2 days of stock left. I sent the 80 units there to the three Tier A health systems under an approved allocation. No alternate supplier or company substitute is available. Supply can't recover before 2026-11-26.

No trusted playbook matched, so I followed the Supply Disruption Response process (SDR-1.1 to 5.1).

**What I found**
- **The late order:** the next ship date is purchase order PO005791 — 4,200 of Polysorbate 80 (RM-221), promised for 2026-10-07. S-104 has two more open orders: PO000369 (RM-221, 3,300, due 10-29) and PO000430 (RM-222, due 10-26).
- **Products affected:** RM-221 feeds Lacrivia 0.1% 5 mL and 10 mL (FG-1001/1002), Cyclosporine OS 0.05% 5 mL (FG-1003) and 11 lens-care products (FG-3001 to FG-3011). An older BOM link that has been replaced was ignored.
- **No backup supplier:** the only other supplier listed, S-131, is not qualified and not approved in the supplier portal. So I raised no purchase requisition.
- **Stock against safety stock (latest snapshot, 2026-09-25):**

| Pack | DC-EAST on hand | DC-EAST safety stock | Days of supply |
|---|---|---|---|
| Lacrivia 5 mL | 46 | 471 | about 1.3 |
| Lacrivia 10 mL | 34 | 233 | about 2.3 |

  DC-CENTRAL and DC-WEST are above safety stock on all three packs. Cyclosporine OS is also above safety stock at DC-EAST (615 vs 252).
- **Recovery:** it takes 50 days from the material shipping to stock reaching the DC (MES standard times; includes the 14-day sterility test). So recovery is no earlier than 2026-11-26, and later by however long S-104 slips.
- **Substitute (BR-SUB-01/02):** none. Both Lacrivia packs are short at DC-EAST, and Cyclosporine OS is made from the same material. Medical Affairs guides therapeutic alternatives.

**Actions taken**
1. **Approval APR-14D2A743 (approved):** the DC-EAST plan totals 80 units, $45,840 at list price, which is over the $25,000 threshold (BR-APPR-01).
2. **Allocations:** units are split by contract tier, then pro rata by 13-week prescription volume (TRx) from prescribers in DC-EAST states, 2026-07-03 to 09-25. Tier A used up all the stock (BR-ALLOC-01/02); no patient-level data was used.

| Allocation | Pack | Riverbend (AC00059) | Oak Hollow (AC00038) | Northfield (AC00117) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| AL-D570A661 | 5 mL | 20 | 15 | 11 |
| AL-CEC5B4FE | 10 mL | 15 | 11 | 8 |

3. **Account team tasks:** CRM-ABB4BC05 (Riverbend), CRM-8AC7CC9F (Oak Hollow), CRM-921C2892 (Northfield), CRM-B57DA1E5 (Clearview, Tier B, none) and CRM-D81F1D82 (Sunridge, Tier B, none). Each covers the allocation, the recovery date and the lack of a substitute.
4. **CASE-8D8F0C47 (Trade Relations):** asks them to notify the wholesalers W-01 Keystone and W-02 Atlas. The wholesaler EDI channel has no API.
5. **CASE-1ABA63F9 (Medical Affairs):** guidance on therapeutic alternatives.
6. **CASE-3F9D947A (Supply Planning):**
   - get a revised ship date from S-104, and flag PO000369 as at risk;
   - consider speeding up S-131's qualification;
   - assess the lens-care products;
   - watch DC-CENTRAL and DC-WEST.

**Not done, and why**
- **Lens-care products:** they have no DC inventory data and no NDC in the commercial data, so I couldn't check them against safety stock or allocate them. Handed to Supply Planning.
- **Other accounts:** I didn't notify the accounts without a supply contract that prescribe Lacrivia in DC-EAST states (8 health-system or independent-clinic accounts). They get no units under the allocation rules, and I read the process step as covering contracted accounts only. The wholesalers are being told through Trade Relations.
- **Other DCs and Cyclosporine OS:** none is below safety stock, so nothing was allocated and there were no transfers between DCs.
- **RM-222 (PO000430):** not part of "the next ship date", so I didn't assess it.

**Assumptions**
- The miss affects PO005791, and S-104 hasn't given a new date, so the recovery date is a floor.
- I placed prescribers in a DC's region by their clinic's state. Riverbend (head office in CA) and the Minnesota health systems count only through their East-state clinics.
- Clearview's Tier B contract (expires 2026-12-31) is treated as still active.
- In the Supply Planning case I said DC-CENTRAL and DC-WEST will likely fall below safety stock before recovery. I didn't calculate that; it's an estimate.

**Knowledge-layer items used:** process Supply Disruption Response; rules BR-ALLOC-01/02, BR-APPR-01, BR-SUB-01/02, BR-LEAD-01, BR-CUST-01, BR-REGION-01, POL-DUA-01; reference sets supply_contracts, list_prices, dc_service_regions, approved_substitutes; and the ratified tables PURCH_ORD, SUPPLIER_MATERIAL, DC_INV, WHSLR_SHIP, PLANT_MATERIAL, RXT_WKLY, PRESCRIBER and ACCOUNT.

sql.sql: SELECT p.PO_ID, p.SUPPLIER_ID, s.SUPPLIER_NM, s.TIER, p.MATERIAL_ID, m.MATERIAL_DESC, m.MATERIAL_TYP, p.ORDER_DT, p.PROMISED_SHIP_DT, p.QTY, p.STATUS FROM dbo.PURCH_ORD p JOIN dbo.SUPPLIER s ON s.SUPPLIER_ID=p.SUPPLIER_ID JOIN dbo.MATERIAL m ON m.MATERIAL_ID=p.MATERIAL_ID WHERE p.SUPPLIER_ID='S-104' AND p.STATUS='OPEN' ORDER BY p.PROMISED_SHIP_DT

SELECT sm.SUPPLIER_ID, s.SUPPLIER_NM, s.TIER, sm.MATERIAL_ID, sm.QUALIFIED_FLG, sm.PRIMARY_FLG FROM dbo.SUPPLIER_MATERIAL sm JOIN dbo.SUPPLIER s ON s.SUPPLIER_ID=sm.SUPPLIER_ID WHERE sm.MATERIAL_ID IN ('RM-221','CMP-310')

WITH l AS (SELECT DC_ID, MATERIAL_ID, MAX(SNAPSHOT_DT) mx FROM dbo.DC_INV WHERE MATERIAL_ID IN ('FG-1001','FG-1002','FG-1003','FG-3001','FG-3002','FG-3003','FG-3004','FG-3005','FG-3006','FG-3007','FG-3008','FG-3009','FG-3010','FG-3011') GROUP BY DC_ID, MATERIAL_ID)
SELECT i.DC_ID, i.MATERIAL_ID, i.SNAPSHOT_DT, i.ON_HAND_UNITS, i.SAFETY_STOCK_UNITS, CASE WHEN i.ON_HAND_UNITS < i.SAFETY_STOCK_UNITS THEN 'BELOW' ELSE 'OK' END st FROM dbo.DC_INV i JOIN l ON l.DC_ID=i.DC_ID AND l.MATERIAL_ID=i.MATERIAL_ID AND l.mx=i.SNAPSHOT_DT ORDER BY i.MATERIAL_ID, i.DC_ID

WITH wks AS (SELECT DISTINCT WK_END_DT FROM PHARMA_DEMO.RAW_3P.RXT_WKLY QUALIFY DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY WK_END_DT DESC) <= 13),
rx AS (SELECT r.PROD_NDC11, p.ACCOUNT_ID clinic_id, SUM(r.TRX_QTY) trx FROM PHARMA_DEMO.RAW_3P.RXT_WKLY r JOIN wks ON wks.WK_END_DT=r.WK_END_DT JOIN PHARMA_DEMO.CORE.PRESCRIBER p ON p.PRSCRBR_ME=r.PRSCRBR_ME WHERE r.PROD_NDC11 IN ('99101010105','99101010110') GROUP BY 1,2),
h AS (SELECT a.ACCOUNT_ID, a.STATE clinic_state, COALESCE(gp.ACCOUNT_ID, pa.ACCOUNT_ID, a.ACCOUNT_ID) top_id FROM PHARMA_DEMO.CORE.ACCOUNT a LEFT JOIN PHARMA_DEMO.CORE.ACCOUNT pa ON pa.ACCOUNT_ID=a.PARENT_ACCOUNT_ID LEFT JOIN PHARMA_DEMO.CORE.ACCOUNT gp ON gp.ACCOUNT_ID=pa.PARENT_ACCOUNT_ID)
SELECT rx.PROD_NDC11, h.top_id, t.ACCOUNT_NM, t.ACCT_TYP, t.STATE top_state, SUM(rx.trx) trx, (SELECT MIN(WK_END_DT)||' to '||MAX(WK_END_DT) FROM wks) wk_range
FROM rx JOIN h ON h.ACCOUNT_ID=rx.clinic_id JOIN PHARMA_DEMO.CORE.ACCOUNT t ON t.ACCOUNT_ID=h.top_id
WHERE h.clinic_state IN ('NY','NJ','PA','MA','FL','GA','NC','OH')
GROUP BY 1,2,3,4,5 ORDER BY 1, trx DESC

SELECT s.WHSLR_ID, w.WHSLR_NM, w.REGION, s.MATERIAL_ID, SUM(s.UNITS) units_28d, MIN(s.SHIP_DT) first_dt, MAX(s.SHIP_DT) last_dt FROM dbo.WHSLR_SHIP s JOIN dbo.WHSLR w ON w.WHSLR_ID=s.WHSLR_ID WHERE s.DC_ID='DC-EAST' AND s.MATERIAL_ID IN ('FG-1001','FG-1002','FG-1003') AND s.SHIP_DT > DATEADD(day,-28,'2026-09-30') GROUP BY s.WHSLR_ID, w.WHSLR_NM, w.REGION, s.MATERIAL_ID ORDER BY s.MATERIAL_ID, units_28d DESC
SELECT pm.PLANT_ID, pm.MATERIAL_ID FROM dbo.PLANT_MATERIAL pm WHERE pm.MATERIAL_ID IN ('RM-221','CMP-310','INT-LC1011','FG-1001','FG-1002','FG-1003','FG-3001') ORDER BY 2,1

escalation_cases.subject: Notify wholesalers W-01 and W-02: Lacrivia supply delay from DC-EAST
escalation_cases.details: The EDI gateway has no API (send_wholesaler_edi is no_api), so this is handed to Trade Relations per SDR-4.2. Please tell the wholesalers served by DC-EAST: Keystone Drug Distributors (W-01) and Atlas Pharma Supply (W-02). Cause: supplier S-104 (Delmar) will miss its 2026-10-07 ship of RM-221 Polysorbate 80 (PO005791). There is no qualified alternate supplier. Impact: DC-EAST is below safety stock on Lacrivia 0.1% 5 mL (NDC 99101-0101-05; 46 on hand vs 471 safety stock, about 1.3 days of supply) and 10 mL (NDC 99101-0101-10; 34 on hand vs 233, about 2.3 days of supply). Remaining DC-EAST units are allocated to Tier A contracted health systems (approval APR-14D2A743; allocations AL-D570A661, AL-CEC5B4FE). Expect short or zero fills on these NDCs from DC-EAST. Recovery: at least 50 days after RM-221 ships (no earlier than 2026-11-26). Cyclosporine OS 0.05% 5 mL is fed by the same material, but DC-EAST stock is currently above safety stock (615 vs 252). DC-CENTRAL and DC-WEST are above safety stock on all three packs.

escalation_cases.subject: Lacrivia shortage at DC-EAST – no approved company substitute; guidance on therapeutic alternatives needed
escalation_cases.details: Per BR-SUB-01 and BR-SUB-02: Lacrivia 0.1% 5 mL and 10 mL are both below safety stock at DC-EAST, so there is no same-brand pack to switch to. The approved company substitute, Cyclosporine OS 0.05% (FG-1003), also depends on the failing material: RM-221 from S-104 goes into CMP-310 and then SEMI-031. So there is no approved company substitute. Please give account teams and customers in DC-EAST states (NY, NJ, PA, MA, FL, GA, NC, OH) guidance on therapeutic alternatives. Expected recovery: no earlier than 2026-11-26.

escalation_cases.subject: S-104 RM-221 delay: revised ship date, S-131 qualification, lens-care exposure not visible in DC inventory
escalation_cases.details: 1) S-104 (Delmar) will miss the 2026-10-07 promised ship of PO005791 (RM-221, 4,200). PO000369 (RM-221, 3,300, due 2026-10-29) is also at risk. Please get a revised ship date from the supplier: recovery at the DC equals ship date + 50 days (MES standard times, BR-LEAD-01). 2) RM-221 is effectively single-source. S-131 (Pinecrest) is listed but QUALIFIED_FLG=N and NOT_APPROVED in the supplier portal, so no requisition was raised. Please consider expediting qualification. 3) RM-221 also feeds 11 lens-care finished goods (FG-3001 to FG-3011) via INT-LC1011 (PL-03) and PL-04. These products have no rows in DC_INV and no commercial NDC data, so I could not check their safety stock or allocate them. Please assess them. 4) Lacrivia allocation at DC-EAST is done (APR-14D2A743, AL-D570A661, AL-CEC5B4FE). DC-CENTRAL and DC-WEST are above safety stock now, but at current run rates they will drop below it before recovery. Please monitor weekly snapshots and re-run the allocation, or consider inter-DC transfers (these need approval).
